title: Agentic Coding: Armin Ronacher
summary: Armin Ronacher live-builds a local transcription tool with Claude Code, showing feedback-loop setup and arguing you must keep your brain on and own the architecture.

assertions.quote: writing code in a tool loop like where it compiles, runs, reads the error, does this. That's the thing that I care about

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: telling an agent and it doesn't really matter which one to create nice software architecture I don't think it really works

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.

assertions.quote: eventually you're going to let through unintentionally because like your brain just turns off a little bit

verdicts.note: Surveys (e.g. Sonar 2026) report many developers don't always check AI code before committing, despite saying they distrust it.

assertions.quote: just to take over your decision-m process, then that part of your brain probably will not be trained

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.

assertions.quote: you can immerse yourself in the output that Claude or any other trendy tool gives you and then hopefully learn something from it

verdicts.note: Agents do speed onboarding and PR summarization, but surveys and the Anthropic learning study show many users skip understanding; outcome depends on use.

assertions.quote: My suspicion is that generally speaking there will be more programmers because it has become easier to create programs

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: I would not I would not ship that app.

verdicts.note: Direction is well supported: greenfield, low-stakes work gets the biggest gains in studies and surveys. The specific multipliers are anecdote.

assertions.quote: none of that is different just because you have an an AI

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.

assertions.quote: I'm mostly doing coding since May and models didn't get better in that period of time

verdicts.note: METR's task-horizon metric kept doubling roughly every 7 months through 2025-26 and coding benchmarks rose sharply; perceived per-release gains feel smaller but the trend is steep.

assertions.quote: some of the open source coding agents with open models and that so far is not really working all that well

verdicts.note: Qwen3-Coder, Kimi K2 and GLM 4.5/4.6 posted strong SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench results in 2025 while generally trailing frontier closed models.

assertions.quote: come with really good documentation tailored towards getting an agent to write it better if it's not in a data set

verdicts.note: Agents parse markdown and commands far more reliably than GUI instructions; llms.txt and markdown docs are spreading for this reason.

assertions.quote: a lot of new software that has to that doesn't exist in a training set

verdicts.note: Studies show LLMs prefer popular libraries and older APIs, but web search and in-context docs partly offset it, and the effect on adoption is not measured.
